notes.text: Maxim Tsyplakov has not dressed for the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters. William Strömgren has taken his spot beside Adam Klapka and Jonathan Castagna.
Connor Zary is out (knee surgery) and has missed the last 16 games.
Jonathan Huberdeau is on injured reserve (hip surgery) and has not played this season. He is a top-six forward.

Kevin Bahl is out for the season and has missed the last 3 games. Joel Hanley has taken his spot beside Šimon Nemec. That pair has had 36% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 38:37 together, down from 46% with Bahl.
William Strömgren was added to the roster on Oct 31 and has played beside Adam Klapka and Jonathan Castagna.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 31% of the team’s shorthanded time in 19 games, up from 2% last season.
A.J. Greer is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and has missed the last 5 games. He is one of their more valuable skaters.

Troy Terry returned in their last game after missing 9 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.
Laurent Brossoit was added to the roster on Nov 3.

ANA.head: Advantage, the Ducks
ANA.body: Even though Calgary gets Honzek back, Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Flames can make it interesting if they keep the shots coming.

CGY.head: Not an easy night for the Flames
CGY.body: Even though Calgary gets Honzek back, Anaheim has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Flames can pull it off if they keep the shots coming.

story.head: Carlsson’s favorite opponent
paras: The Ducks have won two of the three meetings this season. The Flames (8-10-1) lost 3-1 to the Rangers on Wednesday, and the Ducks (10-8-1) lost 4-2 to Nashville the same night. This is a Pacific Division matchup, with the Flames sixth (tied for 25th in the NHL) and the Ducks third (tied for 16th). The Pacific has been the weakest of the four divisions so far.
The Flames’ record (.447) is about what their chances are worth. The Ducks’ record (.553) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.496), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Flames take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd) and take more penalties than they draw (31st). As for the Ducks, they forecheck as hard as almost anyone (2nd), hit a lot (2nd) and give up a lot of dangerous shots (31st). Anaheim has allowed 3.68 goals a game, the third most in the league. The Flames are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Ducks. On top of that, both teams like to play fast, especially the Flames (2nd), so expect an open game.

Joel Farabee (7 G / 10 A / 17 P in 19 GP) leads the Flames in scoring, and Matt Coronato (4 G / 11 A / 15 P in 19 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Ducks, Leo Carlsson (6 G / 20 A / 26 P in 19 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in seven straight games against Calgary. Cutter Gauthier (16 G / 7 A / 23 P in 18 GP) has a team-high 16 goals, tied for third in the NHL, with eleven points in his last five games.

Devin Cooley (5-4-0 / .913 SV% in 9 GS) has been a rock in net for Calgary and will likely start. Lukáš Dostál (4-4-1 / .866 SV% in 10 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Anaheim, but will likely start.
